A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RelCon study. Their complete 19-page documents, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v4 reports original RelCon evaluations for gait regression, activity recognition and public benchmarks, plus component, loss-function and matched-backbone experiments.

after.justification: v5 retains original RelCon results in Tables 1–5 and the appendix confusion matrices, despite removing some experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed distance-learning architecture, augmentations, sparsemax, candidate-based normalization, relative contrastive objective and ResNet-34 encoder remain unchanged. Added similarity and ablation-loss formulas clarify existing computations rather than establish a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six datasets and task coverage. The AHMS description changes from 14 to 16 activities, but v4's figures already contain the same 16 classes. Likewise, changing four walking tasks to three matches the three tasks already enumerated in v4; neither establishes changed coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 removes the RelCon-architecture and Yuan-architecture training-from-scratch comparators. The other principal comparator suites remain unchanged. MAE, CPC and Autoencoder receive more explicit descriptions in v5 but already participated in v4 Table 4; the softer/harder loss comparators also already appeared in v4.

E3.justification: v5 removes the training-from-scratch evaluation condition and the separate ResNet-18/1024-dimensional matched-backbone experiment. Section 5.3 also changes the stated sampling ablation from batch members plus an augmented anchor to batch members and their augmentations; unchanged scores do not establish rerunning. Retained splits, metrics, inference windows and training budgets remain stable.

E4.justification: v4 Appendix A.10/Table 7's architecture-controlled comparison disappears, and Table 5 loses the HHAR and PAMAP2 component-ablation columns. This substantially reduces checks on architectural confounding and cross-dataset component effects. The softer/harder loss study is retained by moving v4 Appendix A.9/Table 6 into v5 Section 5.3/Table 5.

E5.justification: For gait probes, v5 explicitly describes means and standard deviations over five fits, while removing v4's explicit statement that different seeds were used. Classification repetitions and cross-validation uncertainty reporting remain unchanged; no increased run count or new statistical test is reported.

E6.justification: Entire result blocks disappear: Table 3's scratch results, Table 7's matched-backbone results and two benchmark-ablation columns. Removed findings include matched-backbone PAMAP2 MLP F1 of 62.5 for RelCon versus 72.5 for Yuan. Retained main scores and loss-ablation values are unchanged apart from rounding. v5 additionally claims correlation gaps greater than 0.5, although Table 1 gives 0.0578 and 0.0742.

T1.justification: v5 explicitly defines encoder similarity as an inner product in Section 3.2 and gives the log-ratio objective for the existing metric-loss ablation in Section 5.3. These are limited formal specifications; Equations 1–7 and Appendix A.6's complexity analysis otherwise remain unchanged, with no new proofs.

C1.justification: The main novelty, multitask generalization and performance claims remain substantially the same; state-of-the-art language already appeared in v4. v5's conclusion adds the prospective applicability claim that RelCon could work for other quasi-periodic biosignals.

C2.justification: v5 adds mechanistic explanations contrasting cadence-based velocity prediction with temporally precise DST dynamics, and argues that exact metric-distance matching obscures useful gait features. Its softer-loss interpretation broadens from harming gait regression to harming every task, contradicting the retained positive workout-level result. Existing single-sensor and computational limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 7 changes a future code-release promise into reported public availability of RelCon training, architecture and benchmark-evaluation code at a concrete repository. Appendix A.7 adds Yuan table provenance and explains the MLP-probe naming correspondence. Existing hyperparameters and preprocessing remain available. Repository contents were not independently inspected.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially updates positioning through newer wearable and time-series foundation models, including Narayanswamy, Chronos and MOMENT, and additional biosignal SSL literature. It introduces a specific distinction between minute-level handcrafted features and raw high-frequency motion signals. Earlier temporal-pairing discussion and several associated citations are removed; these are substantive literature changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, experimental narrative, discussion and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v5 introduces an explicit contribution list, relocates baseline descriptions, reorders appendix sections, integrates the loss-ablation discussion into the main text and adds acknowledgments.

P2.justification: The empirical presentation is substantially reorganized: Figures 1–2 exchange positions and the t-SNE display is reformatted; Table 3 moves and loses rows; old Tables 5–6 merge into a differently structured Table 5; Table 7 disappears. Confusion matrices move within the appendix and captions are revised. The DST, ROC and confusion-matrix graphics themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Clearer exposition and reported code availability are benefits, but v5 removes useful architecture and training-from-scratch controls and cross-dataset ablations. It also introduces statements contradicting retained tables, including the exaggerated correlation gaps and the claim that softer loss hurts every task despite a 1.39% workout-level gain. These losses in evidential completeness and accuracy outweigh the presentation gains, while the unchanged main method and core results limit the deterioration.
